driver: Members of a pool leave at their own steady rates, which differ widely, so the fast leavers go first and the pool's overall leaving rate falls as its members age; while new members kept arriving the overall rate held high, and once admission stops the closed pool sheds its newest members and then slows, so carrying the open pool's rate overstates the forward losses, and because the record opens part-way through most members' lives, the rate by tenure has to count each member from when the record first sees them.
driver_concrete: Most of Millrind's new volunteer reviewers stop within months (about 9 per cent a month in their first year of access) while reviewers past their third year stop at well under one per cent, so while grants ran at about 320 a month the pool's overall lapse rate held near 3 per cent; review access became invitation-only on 1 September 2026, so the 10,607 reviewers active then are the 2027 pool, shedding their first-year reviewers fast and then slowing, which the open pool's lapse rate overstates; the roster opens in January 2024, so the stop rate by tenure counts each reviewer from the first month the platform shows them active.
stump: Carrying each site's reviewer pool from September 2026 at its own lapse rate of the last two years, with no new reviewers since access became invitation-only, files 41 FTE (40 on the last twelve months' rate, 38 on the last three); the step that lands it there is reading one stop rate off a pool that was still taking in newcomers, when reviewers stop at about 9 per cent a month in their first year and under one per cent from their fourth: carried on the stop rate of each reviewer's own tenure, counted from when the roster first sees them, the 10,607 active reviewers average about 8,800 a month in 2027 and the request is 32 FTE (27 with the tenure curve read from each grant date).
analyst_test: A strong analyst who builds each site's capacity right (the reviews a reviewer completes when the inbox outruns the pool, about 40 a month, against the 2027 inbox the plan implies) and reads the handbook's invitation-only clause carries each site's pool from September 2026 at its own lapse rate of the last two years with no new reviewers and files 41 FTE (40 on twelve months, 38 on three); reviewers stop at rates that fall steeply with tenure, so the closed pool sheds its newest reviewers first, and carried on each reviewer's own tenure the request is 32.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a closed volunteer cohort's 2027 survival, forecast the way product analytics forecasts a retained-user cohort (survival by tenure read from a truncated, censored roster and applied to the members who are left, rather than a pooled churn rate), times the activity a retained reviewer delivers when work outruns the pool; with another field's nouns (a hospital's agency nurses, a utility's call centre) there is no self-selecting volunteer cohort whose members drift away at rates that differ by tenure, so the forecast has nothing to stand on.

lineage.fate: solved, FAILED_TO_STUMP on the portal (2026-10-27): both responses filed 35 FTE, the then golden, by building each site's capacity against its inbox at the saturated pace and carrying each pool at its own lapse rate with almost no new reviewers; the capacity framing was the strong solver's default, so loop 3 moved the decisive step to how the pool is carried
lineage.driver: Work reaches a paid tier only when a volunteer tier falls short, and the volunteer tier's capacity shows only in the periods it fell short, since in every other period it handled everything that arrived; with almost no new volunteers arriving, each pool shrinks at a steady exit rate, so units whose records show almost nothing reaching the paid tier cross below their arrivals inside the forward window, while a share of arrivals carried forward, a trend in the paid work, or capacity read from recent throughput each misses the crossing.
lineage.driver_concrete: Every community review item at Millrind goes first to the volunteer reviewers and reaches the paid moderators only if no volunteer has reviewed it 72 hours after it entered the inbox; volunteers review at their own pace when the inbox is full and below it when it runs dry, so their pace shows only in months when items were routed (most sites in 2022, Security, Embedded & Hardware and Scientific Computing since 2025), and since almost no member has been granted review access after autumn 2024 every site's pool shrinks by about two per cent a month, which takes Data & ML, Databases, Infrastructure & DevOps and Game Development, with almost nothing routed since January 2024, below their 2027 inbox arrivals.
lineage.stump: Carrying each site's paid queue hours per question over the last twelve months onto the 2027 question plan files a request of 23 FTE (25 to 28 with each site's routed share or its monthly paid hours trended forward), inside finance's 26-FTE envelope; the step that lands it there is treating routed items as a share of arrivals, when they are the arrivals each site's shrinking reviewer pool cannot review at the pace reviewers keep when the inbox is full, which puts four sites that have routed almost nothing since January 2024 short of their 2027 inbox and files 35 (31 with the pool trended over the platform's whole record, 53 with the pace read from 2026 throughput).
